written.headline: Nvidia privately confirmed it could track chips to fight smuggling
written.summary: Nvidia representatives privately told U.S. Representative Bill Foster that the company could implement anti-smuggling chip tracking measures. This private acknowledgment contrasts with public industry opposition to the proposed Chip Security Act.

written.headline: US officials disagree on whether Alice Huang spied for China
written.summary: U.S. officials disagree on whether Megaspeed executive Alice Huang spied for China, with some intelligence personnel stating current evidence is inconclusive. Meanwhile, Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang is no longer CEO following reports of affairs and federal investigations into chip sales.

written.headline: ByteDance plans $6B share buyback at $400B valuation
written.summary: ByteDance plans to buy back up to $6 billion worth of shares from existing investors at a valuation of approximately $400 billion. This represents a 20% increase in valuation compared to its 2025 buyback.

written.headline: Senate Banking Chair Tim Scott asks Jensen Huang and Howard Lutnick to testify
written.summary: Senate Banking Chairman Tim Scott invited former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to appear at separate hearings in December regarding national security concerns. Lutnick agreed to appear before the panel next month.

written.headline: Google and Warby Parker debut Gemini-powered smartglasses starting at $395
written.summary: Google, Samsung, and eyewear designers Warby Parker and Gentle Monster have launched Gemini-powered smartglasses starting at $395 with privacy features including a recording notification light. Warby Parker's glasses are available for pre-order starting Thursday, with frames designed by Warby Parker and Gentle Monster.

written.headline: Ethan Mollick's lab releases open-source Primer simulation system
written.summary: Ethan Mollick's Generative AI Lab released Primer, an open-source agent-driven system that converts teacher-led lessons into playable student simulations. The system's paper, prompts, and code are publicly available.

written.headline: Trump defends Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang amid intelligence and chip sale probe
written.summary: US President Donald Trump defended Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang after reports of his relationship with a former executive suspected of gathering intelligence for Beijing. Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation, while US authorities and lawmakers examine national security implications and past chip sales to China.
